title: The expert's checking routine
goal: Run a fast, repeatable check on any AI output — spot the claim, decide if it's checkable, check it, then use, fix or drop it.

blocks.title: Check the right things, fast
blocks.body:
Here's what surprises people: experts don't distrust everything. That would be exhausting, and you'd never finish a worksheet.

What they do is triage. They glance at an output and instantly sort it: this bit is opinion or phrasing — fine. This bit is a factual claim someone could be misled by — that one gets checked. The skill isn't suspicion. It's knowing which few things to check, and doing it in seconds.

blocks.prompt: Put the checking routine in order — the four moves an expert makes on a fresh AI answer:

items.text: Check the checkable ones — quick search, trusted source, or your own knowledge
Spot the claim — what here is stated as a fact?
Decide — use it, fix it, or drop it
Ask — can this actually be checked, or is it just phrasing?

blocks.question: You ask AI for a worksheet fact and it writes: "According to a 2021 Cambridge study, students who chew gum score 15% higher in exams." You like it. What do you do?

options.text: Include it — Cambridge is a trusted name and 15% is specific
Catch it — that's an unverifiable claim; find the real study first, or drop the line entirely
Bump it to 20% so it lands harder with the class

blocks.explanation: Caught it. 👏 A famous name and a neat percentage are exactly the costume a made-up claim wears. No verifiable source, no place in your worksheet — you just protected your class from a myth.

blocks.question: How ready do you feel to run a quick check on any AI output?
